:::{#def-inv-surv-fn}

#### Inverse survival function

Given a [random time-to-event variable](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-random-variable) $T$ with
survival function $\surv(t)$ (@def-surv-fn),
the **inverse survival function** (ISF),
also called the **survival quantile function** (SQF),
$\surv^{-1}(p)$
is the earliest time $t$ at which the survival probability
has fallen to or below $p$:

$$\surv^{-1}(p) \eqdef \inf\cb{t \ge 0 : \surv(t) \le p}, \quad 0 < p < 1.$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-inv-surv-exp}
##### Exponential distribution

For an [exponential distribution](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-exponential) with rate $\haz > 0$,
the survival function is $\surv(t) = \ef{-\haz t}$.

Setting $\surv(t) = p$ and solving for $t$:

$$
\ba
\ef{-\haz t} &= p\\
-\haz t &= \logf{p}\\
t &= \frac{-\logf{p}}{\haz},
\ea
$$

so the inverse survival function of the exponential distribution is:

$$\surv^{-1}(p) = \frac{-\logf{p}}{\haz}.$$

:::{#fig-isf-exp-rates}

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
library(ggplot2)

p_seq <- seq(0.001, 0.999, length.out = 500)
rates <- c(0.5, 1, 2, 4)

df_isf <- do.call(rbind, lapply(rates, function(lam) {
  data.frame(
    p = p_seq,
    isf = -log(p_seq) / lam,
    lambda = factor(
      paste0("λ = ", lam),
      levels = paste0("λ = ", rates)
    )
  )
}))

ggplot(df_isf, aes(x = p, y = isf, color = lambda)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    x = expression(p),
    y = expression(S^{-1}*(p)),
    color = NULL
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

Exponential inverse survival function $\surv^{-1}(p) = -\log(p)/\haz$
for various rate parameters $\haz$.

:::

:::{#thm-inv-surv-is-quantile}
#### Inverse survival function is the quantile function

The inverse survival function equals the $(1-p)$th
[population quantile](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-quantile-function)
of $T$:

$$\surv^{-1}(p) = Q(1 - p),$$

where $Q(u) = \inf\cb{t : \cdf(t) \ge u}$ is the quantile function of $T$.

:::

::: proof

Since $\surv(t) = 1 - \cdf(t)$,

$$
\ba
\surv(t) \le p
&\iff 1 - \cdf(t) \le p\\
&\iff \cdf(t) \ge 1 - p.
\ea
$$

Therefore,

$$
\surv^{-1}(p)
= \inf\cb{t \ge 0 : \surv(t) \le p}
= \inf\cb{t \ge 0 : \cdf(t) \ge 1-p}.
$$

Since $T \ge 0$ almost surely, $\cdf(t) = 0 < 1-p$ for all $t < 0$
(using $p < 1$), so no $t < 0$ satisfies $\cdf(t) \ge 1-p$;
hence the constraint $t \ge 0$ is redundant and can be dropped:

$$
\inf\cb{t \ge 0 : \cdf(t) \ge 1-p}
= \inf\cb{t : \cdf(t) \ge 1-p}
= Q(1-p).
$$

:::
